extracted.intended_audience: competitive students training for national or international mathematical olympiads (students with proof experience)
extracted.subtask_description: A textbook (Euclidean Geometry in Mathematical Olympiads, EGMO) aimed at students preparing for national/international math olympiads; describes scope, prerequisites, solutions availability, errata, translations, and supporting resources. The page functions as a book landing/overview and maintenance page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended audience / purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Written for competitive students training for national or international mathematical olympiads.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book is a comprehensive problem-solving book in Euclidean geometry aimed at olympiad training; this determines level, selection of problems, and exposition style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerequisites
rubrics_metrics.description: It has no prerequisites other than a good deal of courage: any student with proof experience should be able to follow the exposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EGMO is entirely self-contained; the main limiting factor is the ability to read proofs rather than prior geometry theorems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-contained exposition
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the design goals was self-containment so readers need not know existing geometry theorems to follow the exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content scope (problems and figures)
rubrics_metrics.description: The book has a selection of about 300 problems from around the world and about 250 figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets expectations for breadth and density of practice material and visual support in the textbook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solutions coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Solutions to about a quarter of the practice problems in the back of the textbook are provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Space constraints limited the number of included solutions; for problems without provided solutions, readers are directed to hints, online resources, or forums.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hints design principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Each problem in the text has one or more hints; the intention is that the union of all the hints should form an outline of the complete solution (even if the details are omitted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hints are meant to collectively outline full solutions so that motivated readers can complete the proofs; they are a pedagogical tool rather than full worked solutions in all cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Errata reporting and management
rubrics_metrics.description: There is an errata list (PDF and TeX) and 'Instructions for submitting errata'; the author notes the errata list is extensive and highlights several important corrections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides an explicit channel and documentation for identifying and correcting mistakes; the page enumerates specific significant errata (with page numbers and correction details) to alert readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources and attribution for problems
rubrics_metrics.description: The author included sources for as many of the problems as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readers can look up corresponding threads on Art of Problem-Solving’s Contest Index or the user-created forum linked on the page to find discussions/solutions; sourcing facilitates further research and verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for finding additional solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: If stuck on a problem with no solution in the book, consult (a) the hints in the text, (b) the Automatically Generated EGMO Solutions Treasury, (c) a user-created forum with a link to discussion for every problem, (d) Art of Problem-Solving’s Contest Index threads, or (e) post on AoPS forums.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists multiple external resources and strategies for obtaining solutions and community help, acknowledging the limited number of official solutions included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation & permission policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Contact reprint-permission [at] ams.org if interested in a translation; the author has preemptively granted blanket author-approval to the AMS to move forward with any translation proposals (dated 22 April 2023).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies the procedural route and preapproval status for translations, streamlining legitimate translation efforts through the AMS contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendations / complementary resources
rubrics_metrics.description: The page recommends other geometry textbooks (e.g., A Beautiful Journey Through Olympiad Geometry, Lemmas in Olympiad Geometry, UKMT Plane Euclidean Geometry) as supplementary or alternative learning paths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggests alternative texts for different pacing or entry points (e.g., a slower ramp-up for beginners), helping readers choose materials matching their background.
